youtube.title: Why a Cat's Tongue Feels Like Sandpaper 🐱 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
A cat's tongue is covered in tiny spikes called papillae, made of keratin, the same protein as your fingernails. A 2018 study in PNAS showed that each one is a hollow, backward-curved scoop that draws saliva deep into the fur when the cat grooms. They act like a built-in comb and brush at the same time, cleaning all the way down to the skin.
